title: Turning Personal Loss into Purpose: James Harrell as 2026 Pee Dee Heart Walk Chair
summary: According to the American Heart Association (AHA), 9 out of 10 people experiencing cardiac arrest outside a hospital will not survive. Yet immediate CPR can double or triple chances of survival, underscoring the critical importance of knowing how to respond when every second counts.
body_markdown:
According to the[American Heart Association (AHA)](https://cpr.heart.org/en/resources/cpr-facts-and-stats/) , 9 out of 10 people experiencing cardiac arrest outside a hospital will not survive. Yet immediate CPR can double or triple chances of survival, underscoring the critical importance of knowing how to respond when every second counts.


James Harrell participates in pie-in-the-face fundraiser on Sonoco Family Day AHA charity event Sept. 19, 2026


It’s the kind of information that led Global Industrial Paper Packaging President of Sonoco,[James Harrell,](https://www.sonoco.com/leadership/james-harrell-iii) to accept a position as Chair of the[2026 Pee Dee Heart Walk](https://www2.heart.org/site/TR?pg=entry&fr_id=13201) , a role encompassing more than the annual walk itself, which raised just over **$210,000 against its $300,000** goal so far this year. As chair, James will continue leading engagement efforts among local businesses and community leaders to support year-round AHA activities as well as the expansion of CPR education.


“A few years back, I joined the Association’s Pee Dee board as another Sonoco executive, Roger Fuller, had been set to retire,” said James. “That’s when I began learning more and more about the organization and how they impact people, especially here in the Southeast where we have some of the highest rates of cardiovascular disease, stroke and heart failure.”


The Southeast has historically been designated the “Stroke Belt,” with death rates from stroke significantly higher than other parts of the country. The AHA attributes the disparity, in part, to underlying health risk factors, but in James’ experience, cardiac emergencies can affect anyone.


“When you think ‘heart attack,’ you immediately think of older people or those who’re overweight or generally unhealthy, but over 90% of people have been directly or indirectly impacted through a close family member or friend and I’m one of them.”


At a young age, James’ childhood friend died of a heart attack. He was just 13 years old.


James Harrell prepares for a dunk tank at Sonoco Family Day Spet. 19, 2026, to raise money for AHA.


“He was with a group of friends, and I happened to be driving through town when I saw his mom’s car fly by,” said James. “I knew something was wrong when I saw a crowd gathered at the local Hardee’s. No one attempted CPR before EMS arrived.”


“Could it \[bystander CPR\] have saved his life?” James asked. “I’m not sure. But what I do know is we need to teach people CPR and empower them to use it when needed, along with other life-saving equipment, such as defibrillators, which we need more of in schools and public places.”


The[Pee Dee Regional Community Training Center](https://pdctc.com/) equips thousands of residents each year with lifesaving Hands-Only CPR training as well as the skills needed to operate automated external defibrillators (AEDs). Events like the Heart Walk help provide local funding for these programs and keep CPR education accessible in the community.


“You get involved, you start hearing the statistics and you go, oh, I get why we all need to band together to do our part to keep the AHA focused on the day-to-day activities that truly save lives.”


Thousands of people will be joining James at the Heart Walk in Florence this Saturday, October 24, to help close the gap. Whether by participating or making a contribution, every effort can help strengthen CPR education and heart-health initiatives across the Pee Dee.
